descriptor.scene: A grey rainy afternoon: rain runs down the four-pane window and the light in the shed is flat and cool, with the bare bulb doing the work. On the bench in the foreground lies a RUINED PLANE, gone soft and limp, its creases collapsed. At the NEAR RIGHT END of the line, Mira is fitting the small new felt-fingered machine into place with a screwdriver, and Pip stands beside her holding out a screw in one hand, leaning in and helping. Both are absorbed and practical about it. The rest of the line stands unchanged behind them. It is grey and cosy, NOT gloomy and NOT dramatic. CRITICAL: there is EXACTLY ONE Pip in this image and it is the small tin toy standing ON THE BENCH TOP beside Mira, no taller than her forearm is long. There is NO second robot, NO larger robot, and NOTHING standing on the floor. Pip NEVER appears twice and is NEVER as tall as the workbench. CAMERA LAW: the workbench is BUILT AGAINST THE WINDOW WALL, so the camera stands in the open floor of the room and Mira is at the bench seen FROM BEHIND or FROM THE SIDE, working away from the viewer with the window in front of her. She is NOT standing behind the bench facing the camera across it: there is no floor on that side.

The door is in the SHORT wall facing the yard. ONE SQUARE FOUR-PANE WINDOW sits in the LONG wall, with a WORKBENCH running the full length of that wall beneath it. Shelves and a pegboard above the bench. A single bare bulb on a flex. Outside the door, a LOW CONCRETE STEP of two treads; beyond it a mown grass yard about fifteen metres long ending in a WAIST-HIGH WOODEN GATE, which is the far marker the first plane reaches.
